what_its_for: This combination medicine helps your body get rid of extra fluid and salt through your urine. It is used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure, and swelling (edema) caused by conditions like liver disease or kidney problems. Keeping blood pressure under control helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney damage.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, with or without food. Taking it with food or milk can help prevent an upset stomach. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Because this medicine makes you urinate more often, take it in the morning or early afternoon so it does not keep you up at night. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and how your body responds. A common starting dose for adults is one tablet (25 mg spironolactone / 25 mg hydrochlorothiazide) taken once or twice daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose over time. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day or close to your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of high-potassium foods such as bananas, oranges, potatoes, tomatoes, and salt substitutes that contain potassium — spironolactone can raise your potassium levels to a dangerous level. Avoid alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Avoid standing up too quickly, especially in hot weather or after exercise, as this medicine can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Do not take over-the-counter NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without asking your doctor first, as they can reduce how well this medicine works and affect your kidneys. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as hydrochlorothiazide can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: muscle weakness, cramps, or numbness (signs of potassium problems); irregular or fast heartbeat; extreme dizziness or fainting; decreased urination or no urination; sudden weight gain or severe swelling; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing; signs of low sodium such as headache, confusion, or feeling very weak; or unusual tiredness. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting this medication.
when_it_works: You may start urinating more within the first few hours of taking your first dose. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks to feel the full blood pressure-lowering effect of this medicine. Even if you feel well, keep taking it every day as prescribed. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking this medicine without your doctor's guidance.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to dizziness and the risk of falls — rise slowly from sitting or lying positions. Pregnant women: This medicine is generally NOT recommended during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding women: Both medicines can pass into breast milk; talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. People with kidney or liver disease: Use with caution — your doctor will monitor your kidney function and electrolytes (sodium, potassium) regularly. People with diabetes: Hydrochlorothiazide may raise blood sugar levels; monitor your blood sugar more closely and report any changes to your doctor.
